paper.title: Contextual Multi-armed Bandit Algorithm for Semiparametric Reward Model

settings.name_in_paper: Semiparametric contextual MAB (semiparametric additive reward model)
unmapped: Expected reward is nu(t) + b_i(t)^T mu, where the linear part is time-invariant and the intercept nu(t) is an arbitrary (possibly history-dependent / adversarial) action-independent term with |nu(t)| <= 1; regret does not depend on nu(t)
Each of the N arms has its own context vector b_i(t) in R^d at each round
settings.definition_quote:
Given $\mathcal{F}_{t-1}$, we assume that the expectation of the reward $r_i(t)$ can be decomposed into a time-invariant, linear component depending on action $(b_i(t)^T\mu)$ and a nonparametric component depending on time and possibly on $\mathcal{F}_{t-1}$, but not on the action ($
u(t)$): \mathbb{E}(r_i(t)|\mathcal{F}_{t-1})=
u(t)+b_i(t)^T\mu. ... the error $\eta_i(t)$ is $R$-sub-Gaussian ... $||b_i(t)||_2\leq 1,~ ||\mu||_2\leq 1,~ |
u(t)|\leq 1$

algorithms.name: Proposed TS algorithm (semiparametric Thompson sampling with centered contexts)

source.label: mainthm
source.quote: Under (\ref{semipara}), (\ref{error2}), and (\ref{bounddness}), the regret of Algorithm \ref{prop_alg} is bounded as follows. For $\forall \delta\in (0,1)$, with probability $1-\delta$, \begin{align*}R(T)&\leq O\big(d^{3/2}\sqrt{T}\sqrt{\mathrm{log}(Td)\mathrm{log}(T/\delta)}\big(\sqrt{\mathrm{log}(1+T/d)}+\sqrt{\mathrm{log}(1/\delta)}\big)\big).\end{align*}

results.notes: Regret is sum of b_{a*}^T mu - b_{a(t)}^T mu (means), held with probability 1-delta. Algorithm uses T, d, R and delta in v. Computation O(N) per round as claimed (pi_i(t) computed per arm).
